headline: Kept 4% of replacement cost new for second homes until Fiscal Year 2030 audit; signed Motor Vehicle Commitment 26-04.
summary: Members also discussed raising the exemption limit from $3,000 to $5,000, which would need to go before Town Meeting. Real estate values will be adjusted using sales from January through December 2025. The Wilkinsonville Water District wants to meet to vote on cutting its budget before its tax rate is set.

decision_titles: Open and executive session minutes of August 4, 2026
4% of replacement cost new for second homes
plain_text:
TOWN OF SUTTON
BOARD OF ASSESSORS
 4 UXBRIDGE ROAD
SUTTON, MA  01590-1702
  508-865-8722
                     Meeting Minutes – August 11, 2026
Present:  Robert Nunnemacher, Chairman
    Matthew Read, Assessor
               Tracey Tardy, Principal Assessor
 
 Meeting called to order at 5:00 p.m.
1.         The Board voted unanimously to accept the open session meeting minutes and executive session
            meeting minutes of August 4, 2026
2.         Old & New Business
The Board discussed second homes and voted to keep the 4% of replacement cost new, which is used now, until next
audit in Fiscal Year 2030.  There is not a local option regarding eliminating second home personal property tax
 pursuant to Massachusetts General Laws (MGL) 59, Section 5 Clause 20
The Chairman spoke to the Board regarding Supplemental billing – currently there are twelve (12) pro rata billings
The Board discussed possibly changing the exemption limit from $3,000 to $5,000 but this would need to go before Town 
Meeting
The Principal Assessor informed the Board that she has spoken to Shelley Gorman, Clerk for Wilkinsonville Water District
regarding setting their tax rate – the water district would like to schedule a meeting to discuss and vote on reducing their
budget before setting the tax rate
Principal Assessor will have the real estate values adjusted this week to reflect sales from January through December 2025
- one year sales for single family and condominium classifications and all other classes of property two years of sales were 
used
3.         Decisions & Actions Taken
The Board signed the Motor Vehicle Commitment 26-04
4.         Adjourned Open Session @ 5:45 to enter into Executive Session regarding
            Abatements/Exemptions
The Board entered into executive session to review abatement and/or exemption applications pursuant
to Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 59, Section 60, and Chapter 30A, Section 21, Item number 7. We are meeting in executive session 
to comply with Chapter 59, Section 60, which limits inspection of Chapter 59 abatement and exemption applications to assessors and the 
deputies, clerks and assistants of the assessors, and certain other parties listed in the law. Chapter 30A, Section 21, Item number 7 permits 
public bodies to meet in executive session for the purpose of complying with general laws. 
The Board of Assessors adjourned its open meeting at or about 5:45 p.m. 
Respectfully Submitted,
Linda Hicks, Assistant Assessor
